note: Boundary lines and regions for the subcontinent. Defined once, referenced by claims. See canonical/regions/schema.md.

lines.name: Krishna river
lines.basis: Traced west to east from the source at Mahabaleshwar in the Western Ghats through Karad, Sangli and the Almatti reach, past Srisailam, to the delta below Vijayawada. Historical atlases put the Vijayanagara-Bahmani frontier on this river and its tributary the Tungabhadra; the doab between the two was fought over for two centuries.

lines.name: Tungabhadra river
lines.basis: The Krishna's southern tributary, running from the Ghats past Hampi to its confluence. Vijayanagara's capital sat on its south bank, and the doab between the two rivers was the ground both powers fought over for two centuries.

lines.name: Narmada river
lines.basis: Runs east to west across central India to the Gulf of Khambhat. The conventional dividing line between north India and the Deccan in Indian historiography.

lines.name: Tapti river
lines.basis: South of and parallel to the Narmada, reaching the sea at Surat. The Khandesh corridor between them was the usual route between Gujarat and the Deccan.

lines.name: Vindhya and Satpura ranges
lines.basis: The hill country flanking the Narmada, the physical barrier the river line stands for.

lines.name: Himalayan front
lines.basis: The southern edge of the range, where the plains end. Polities of the plains stop here; Himalayan kingdoms sit above it.

lines.name: Eastern edge of the Indus basin
lines.basis: The Thar desert margin, which separated Sindh and the lower Indus from the Gangetic plain and Rajasthan.

lines.name: Western edge of the Bengal delta
lines.basis: The Rajmahal gap and the Chota Nagpur upland, the approach by which Bengal was invaded and the line its independent sultanate held.

lines.name: Eastern edge of Gujarat
lines.basis: The Aravalli foothills and the upper Sabarmati, the landward boundary of the Gujarat sultanate.

lines.name: Chambal and the Malwa scarp
lines.basis: The Chambal valley and the northern edge of the Malwa plateau, the usual division between the Gangetic plain and Malwa.

lines.name: Aravalli range
lines.basis: Runs south-west to north-east across Rajasthan; the Rajput states sat along and behind it.

lines.name: Northern Eastern Ghats
lines.basis: The hill line inland of the Orissa and northern Andhra coast, the landward edge of the Kalinga polities.

lines.name: Vindhya and Kaimur scarp
lines.basis: The southern edge of the Gangetic plain east of the Chambal, where the plain meets the Vindhya and Kaimur hills. Awadh and the Jaunpur sultanate lie north of it.

lines.name: Eastern limit of the Deccan plateau
lines.basis: The Eastern Ghats above the Godavari delta, where the plateau drops to the coastal plain. The Bahmani frontier faced Warangal and the Reddi kingdoms of the Krishna-Godavari coast; it did not run to the Bay of Bengal, which is where a band drawn only between the Tapti and the Krishna ends up.

lines.name: Yamuna, plains reach
lines.basis: Traced from OpenStreetMap, not from memory. The Yamuna below the Himalayan gorge, from the Delhi reach to the confluence at Prayagraj. OSM relation for the Yamuna (waterway=river), restricted to the points below 28.2N so the upper Himalayan course does not drag the line north, then reduced to one ordered polyline by binning at a quarter degree of longitude and taking the median latitude of each bin. Bundelkhand is classically the country between this river and the Vindhyas.

lines.name: Brahmaputra, Assam reach
lines.basis: Traced from OpenStreetMap, not from memory. The Brahmaputra across the Assam valley, from the Goalpara reach to the Sadiya head. Same OSM relation and same binning as the Yamuna, restricted to points east of 90.8E and below 28N -- the relation also carries the Yarlung Tsangpo across Tibet at about 29N and the Jamuna running south through Bangladesh, and neither belongs to this frontier. The Ahom kingdom article calls the kingdom a state of the Brahmaputra Valley.

lines.name: Indus, Ladakh reach
lines.basis: Traced from OpenStreetMap, not from memory. The Indus between the Tibetan border and the Gilgit reach, the valley Ladakh is built along. Same OSM relation and binning, restricted to points east of 75.5E and north of 32N. The line passes through 77.5E 34.12N, which is Leh -- the capital sits on the river, which is a useful check that the trace is the real course.

regions.name: The peninsula south of the Krishna and Tungabhadra
regions.basis: Vijayanagara's core. The Krishna and its tributary the Tungabhadra were the frontier with the Bahmani sultanate and its successors, contested along the Raichur doab between them. Sri Lanka is cut out: the island had its own kings throughout, and a box reaching the Bay of Bengal otherwise collects it.

regions.name: The Deccan between the Krishna and the Tapti
regions.basis: The Bahmani sultanate's ground: the plateau between the two rivers, stopping at the Eastern Ghats rather than running on to the Bay of Bengal.

regions.name: The Gangetic plain
regions.basis: The plain between the Himalayan front and the Narmada, from the Yamuna eastward. It was clipped to a box reaching 68 east, which put Rajasthan, Gujarat and Sindh inside the Gangetic plain and handed all three to whichever power held Delhi.

regions.name: Bengal
regions.basis: The delta and its approaches, the territory of the independent sultanate from 1352.

regions.name: Gujarat
regions.basis: The peninsula and the plain behind it, the Gujarat sultanate's territory.

regions.name: The Doab and the Punjab
regions.basis: The Jumna-Ganges doab and the rivers west of it — what the Sultanate of Delhi actually held after Timur.

regions.name: Rajputana
regions.basis: The Rajput country as a block. Kept as a named region because several claims reference the area, but no claim draws a single polity across it: Marwar, Mewar, Amber, Bikaner and Jaisalmer were distinct states with their own lines.

regions.name: Malwa
regions.basis: The plateau between the Chambal and the Narmada.

regions.name: Orissa and the Kalinga coast
regions.basis: The coastal strip from the Mahanadi south toward the Godavari.

regions.name: Sindh and the lower Indus
regions.basis: The lower Indus valley and its delta.

regions.name: The eastern Gangetic plain
regions.basis: Awadh and the plain between the Doab and Bengal, bounded south by the Vindhya-Kaimur scarp. The Jaunpur sultanate's ground.

regions.name: The subcontinent below the Himalaya
regions.basis: The ground this claim file speaks for. Inside it the claims are the map and the boundary source is discarded, so a gap here means nobody has authored it rather than that the source said something. The Himalayan front is the northern edge because the mountain kingdoms above it are a separate problem.

regions.name: Sri Lanka
regions.basis: The island. Kotte, Kandy and Jaffna held it; no mainland Indian power of this period ruled there, and Vijayanagara's raids on Jaffna did not annex it.

regions.name: The mainland peninsula south of the Krishna and Tungabhadra
regions.basis: The half-plane south of the Krishna, clipped to the southern mainland rather than to the whole subcontinent box.

regions.name: The land between the Krishna and the Tapti
regions.basis: The band itself, before the eastern limit is applied.

regions.name: The coast east of the Deccan plateau
regions.basis: The coastal plain below the Eastern Ghats, held by the Reddi kingdoms and the Gajapatis, not by the Deccan sultans.

regions.name: Mewar
regions.basis: The southern Aravalli uplands around Chittor, Kumbhalgarh and Udaipur. Mewar was one Rajput state among several; Marwar, Amber, Bikaner and Jaisalmer were separate and are left to the boundary source.

regions.name: Delhi and the upper doab
regions.basis: Delhi, Agra and the Ganges-Jumna doab between them. What was left of the sultanate after Timur: the Sayyids held the capital and its hinterland while Jaunpur, Malwa, Gujarat and the Punjab governors went their own way.

regions.name: Western Rajasthan
regions.basis: Marwar, Bikaner and Jaisalmer — the desert states west of the Aravallis. Delhi raided and took tribute here; it did not administer the country.

regions.name: The Doab and the Punjab, without the desert states
regions.basis: What the sultans of Delhi actually governed. The box that defines the Doab and the Punjab reaches 72 east, which handed Jodhpur to the Lodis.

regions.name: Bundelkhand
regions.basis: The country between the Yamuna and the Vindhyas, which is how Bundelkhand is ordinarily defined. Both lines are traced from OSM. Orchha and Panna sit inside it.

regions.name: The Assam valley
regions.basis: The Brahmaputra valley from the Goalpara reach to Sadiya. A box, and coarse on purpose: it takes in the flanking hill margins the Ahoms contested rather than only the valley floor they administered, and the region resolver has no way to band a corridor around a river. The western limit is 90.6E and not further, because Bhutan and the duars lie beyond it -- an earlier version reached 88E to match what the source calls Assam at 1783 and swallowed Bhutan whole in three snapshots. It is coarser than the kingdom; it is not in Burma, which is where the source puts it.

regions.name: Ladakh
regions.basis: The upper Indus and Shyok basin between the Karakoram and the Great Himalaya. A box: the two ranges are real frontiers but this project has no traced line for either, and inventing one would be worse than admitting the box. The bounds follow the traced Indus reach through Ladakh.

regions.name: The Mysore plateau
regions.basis: The southern Karnataka plateau around Mysore, Srirangapatna and Bangalore. A box, and the weakest extent in this file: Mysore's reach moved a great deal between the Wodeyars and Tipu Sultan and this does not follow it.

regions.name: Marwar
regions.basis: Jodhpur, Barmer, Jalore, Nagaur and Pali -- the districts the Marwar article names -- with Mewar cut out where the boxes meet along the Aravallis. Narrower than sa-marwar, which is the whole desert block including Bikaner and Jaisalmer; those were their own Rathore and Bhati states and are not claimed here.

regions.name: Marwar box
regions.basis: The rectangle sa-marwar-proper starts from, before Mewar is removed. Not meant to be claimed directly.

regions.name: The western Deccan
regions.basis: The Seuna article puts the realm at its peak as stretching from the Narmada in the north to the Tungabhadra in the south, in the western part of the Deccan. Both rivers are already named lines in this file, so the frontier is the one the description gives rather than one drawn to fit.

regions.name: The eastern Deccan
regions.basis: Telangana and coastal Andhra around Warangal. A box: the Kakatiya article gives the reach as most of the eastern Deccan, Telangana and Andhra Pradesh with parts of eastern Karnataka, northern Tamil Nadu and southern Odisha, and that is a description of a territory rather than of a frontier. Coarse and said to be coarse.

regions.name: The Deccan between the Narmada and the Krishna
regions.basis: The Satavahana heartland, holding both capitals the article names: Pratishthana, which is Paithan on the Godavari, and Amaravati on the lower Krishna. The article adds that at times the rule extended into Gujarat, Madhya Pradesh and Karnataka, which this does not attempt to draw.
